methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes SOURCE STRUCTURE (toc_inventory.json / derived/scope_packets/GS.json). Chapter GS is a heavily two-column-TOC-corrupted chapter: the deterministic prepare-scope-chapter tool flagged 2 unresolved headings ('Abdominal Hernia' near GS33, 'Inflammatory Bowel Disease' near GS36 - neither produced a toc_inventory.json node and therefore neither is represented as its own study unit; both are logged in review_items.json as unrecoverable coverage gaps), and 5 additional section/topic nodes independently identified during study-unit construction show clear textual evidence of the same two-column OCR bleed pattern (GS.S12 'Anorectum' containing 4 unrelated Liver topics as T08-T11; GS.S16 'Breast' T01 merging 'Short Gut Syndrome' with 'Benign Breast Lesions'; GS.S17 'Groin Hernias Surgical Endocrinology' merging two section titles with corrupted T-children; GS.S18 'Crohn's Disease Pediatric Surgery' and GS.S19 'Ulcerative Colitis Skin Lesions' each merging two section titles; GS.S21 'Landmark ... Trials' whose T-children are actually Large Bowel Obstruction disease content). Per docs/scope-chapter-workflow.md's resolution order, canonical TOC data and raw_ocr_line were checked for every case (confirming the merges are genuine printed-source artifacts, not extraction bugs); no independent raw-OCR/body-heading corpus beyond toc_inventory.json exists for this project (same limitation documented in chapter G's audit), so body-heading/nearby-page confirmation (steps 3-4) was not available, and each case is resolved either by textually splitting an obvious two-topic merge into separate study units (both citing the same shared source_node_id), by retaining a single legible real-world term found within a corrupted fragment (e.g., 'Appendicitis') with UNRESOLVED page precision, or by explicit UNCERTAIN classification (GS.S17.T02, 'Adrenal Gland') where even the topic identity itself could not be confirmed. No Toronto Notes heading was invented; every study unit traces to specific, legible source-node text.

source_hierarchy_path: GS.S16.T01 (Short Gut Syndrome Benign Breast Lesions)

'Benign Breast Lesions' is the portion consistent with the parent section title ('Breast', GS65-GS70) and is represented as its own study unit; the unrelated 'Short Gut Syndrome' fragment is represented separately (see next unit) since it describes a distinct, unrelated clinical entity bled in from elsewhere in the two-column source page. No independent raw-OCR/body-heading corpus beyond toc_inventory.json exists for this project to relocate either fragment with more precision.

study_units.title: Large Bowel Obstruction (Mechanical and Functional/Ogilvie's Syndrome)
source_hierarchy_path: GS.S21.T02 (Functional Large Bowel Obstruction: Colonic Pseudo-Obstruction References vv eee eee eee eee eee 6578)
study_units.structural_rationale: GS.S21.T01-T03 are extracted as children of a section titled 'Landmark General and Thoracic Surgery Trials', but their actual content (Mechanical Large Bowel Obstruction; Functional Large Bowel Obstruction/Colonic Pseudo-Obstruction; '(Ogilvie's Syndrome)') is unrelated clinical disease content, not trial names - the same documented title/content mismatch pattern as chapter G's SU-G-44 through SU-G-46 (raw_ocr_line for GS.S21 confirms the printed title itself, so this is not treated as an extraction artifact to silently correct). T02's raw title embeds the word 'References', consistent with genuine landmark-trial reference-list content existing somewhere on these pages but not surviving extraction as its own topic; no landmark-trial-specific content could be recovered and none is fabricated here. All three T-nodes are consolidated into one study unit since T02 and T03 are a single split concept (Functional Large Bowel Obstruction = Ogilvie's Syndrome).
